Dokkan Unit Forge optional local video and game-sound converter

converter.js, converter-worker.js, audio-decoder.js and audio-worker.js:
GPL-3.0-or-later.
Copyright 2026 Dokkan Unit Forge contributors.

The independently loaded ffmpeg-core.js and ffmpeg-core.wasm are the unmodified
single-thread @ffmpeg/core 0.12.10 release. Upstream declares GPL-2.0-or-later;
we distribute this converter combination under GPL-3.0-or-later. Individual
third-party files retain their original notices and licensing. No private
server, paid API, device account, or SharedArrayBuffer is required to convert.

AV1 software playback additionally uses unmodified libav.js6.10.9.0 LGPL/BSD
variants av1-opus and webm-vp9-cli. Its libaom decoder works without native AV1
hardware, decoding one IVF packet at a time into a VP8 intermediate before MP4
preparation. 10-bit AV1 is converted to browser-compatible 8-bit output.

Full corresponding upstream sources, including FFmpeg 5.1.4 and9.0, codec libraries,
FFmpeg.wasm bindings/build scripts, Emscripten 3.1.40 and SDL2 2.24.2, are supplied
in the accompanying Dokkan-Unit-Forge-Media-Corresponding-Source.zip. The exact
source revisions and archive SHA256 values are recorded in the adjacent
corresponding-source-manifest.json andlibav-source-manifest.json. Relevant license texts are in licenses/.
Build preparation instructions and pinned source archives are in that ZIP.

The sources match upstream release build references. Mutable references were
resolved to commits older than npm publication; no bit-for-bit reproducibility
claim is made because upstream Docker/system package inputs are not frozen.

This module provides media preparation, not proof that every game movie or
animation has been verified. Preserve this notice and ship corresponding
sources with any redistributed compiled core.

Audio preparation uses the same unmodified FFmpeg core for PCM muxing, gain,
resampling and supported HCA fallback. Common plain ADX is first decoded by the
original native-arithmetic helper into WAV. Actual supplied banks tested here
contain ADX; availability
of a codec does not establish encrypted HCA or every Atom cue is verified.
Original Forge bank parsing/default routing and fixed-origin movie-source helper
are supplied as accompanying application sources with their existing notices.

The portable visual editor uses the same existing unmodified FFmpeg/LibAV WASM
files. Its editor, streaming VP9 and AV1 normalization adapters are original
GPL-3.0-or-later source. The original MIT native-adx.js arithmetic codec writes
plain native-compatible ADX version4 movie sound; FFmpeg's ADX scale convention
and predictor rounding differ from the supplied original CRI decoder. Exact
original native decoder comparisons are documented separately from playback.
Source input/planning/USM writer helpers retain their own notices. All authored
helpers and their hash manifest accompany the corresponding-source archive.

The original MIT hca-metadata.js helper validates bounded HCA headers/frame CRCs,
logical delay/padding and loop sample ranges. Tested HCA2.0 cipher0 and public
static cipher1 sources are copied/normalized, trimmed and polarity-corrected to
match independently executed original game decoding before playback/editing.
Original compressed source bytes are preserved. Static type1 follows the public
MIT VGAudio CriHcaKey permutation, with fresh frame/header CRCs. Tests use original synthetic audio, not copied
game sounds. Other encrypted/untested HCA is not claimed verified. No additional
codec binary is shipped; the same unmodified FFmpeg core decodes HCA payloads.

The original MIT preview-bgm.js and preview-bgm-source.js adapters bind move
music to fixed native metadata and the exact successfully bound Lua source.
They use this existing decoder worker and original AudioBus master/capture;
no new codec binary or original game music is included in this module. Music
is resolved from the user's imported resources or its fixed authorized public
source through the existing preview transport and offline cache. Native codec,
preview graph and capture verification remain separate from actual game mixer,
physical-device and combat testing. The corresponding source includes both
adapters alongside the independent converter's existing GPL license.

Forge stage-recorder.js and stage-record-worker.js are original GPL-3.0-or-later adapters for fixed own-preview native snapshots and local streamed VP9/AAC recording; upstream LibAV/FFmpeg/libvpx retain the licenses listed above. Native snapshot/save controllers and Forge audio/context helpers are original MIT source. No original game music or captured game movies are included in the corresponding-source archive.
